div.head: Episc 6
div.ab: Ne sceall he geþafian ænig unriht ne woh gemet ne fals gewihte; ac hit gebyreð, þæt [b]e his ræde fare ⁊ be his gewitnesse æghwylc lahriht, ge burhriht ge landriht; ⁊ ælc burhgemet ⁊ ælc wægpundern beo be his dihte gescift swiðe rihte, þe læs ænig man oðrum misbeode ⁊ ðurh þæt syngige ealles to swyþe.

Non debet pati (Nec p. d.) aliquod iniustum uel (aliquam circumuentionem) iniuste mensure uel iniusti ponderis; sed conuenit, ut per consilium et testimonium eius omne legis rectum (scitum) et burgi mensura et omne pondus (ponderis) sit secundum dictionem eius institutum ualde rectum, ne quis alium (proximum suum) seducat et per hoc (pro quo) decidat in peccatum.

Ne sceall he geþafian ænig unriht, ne woh gemet ne fals gewiht; ac hit gebyreð þæt be his ræde fare and be his gewitnesse æghwylc lahriht, ge burhriht ge landriht. And ælc burhgemet and ælc wægpundern beo be his dihte gescift swiðe rihte, þe læs ænig man oðrum misbeode and ðurh þæt syngige ealles to swyþe.

Nicht soll er erlauben irgend ein Unrecht, weder unrichtig Maass noch falsch Gewicht; sondern es gebührt sich, dass nach seinem Beschlusse und unter seiner Kenntnissnahme jegliches Satzungsrecht, sowohl Stadtrecht wie Landrecht, gehe; und jedes Stadtmaass und jede Wage sei nach seiner Anordnung genau richtig bestimmt, damit nicht jemand dem anderen Unrecht anthue und dadurch allzu sehr sündige.

He shall not permit any wrong, neither false measure nor false weight; but it is fitting that every statute law, both town law and country law, should proceed by his counsel and with his knowledge; and every town measure and every balance shall be regulated very exactly according to his direction, lest anyone wrong another and thereby sin all too greatly.

He must not permit any injustice, neither an incorrect measurement nor a false weight; but it is proper that every law—both law in the town and law in the country—undergo his review and consent. And every town measurement and every weigh scale is to be properly adjusted under his supervision, lest any man defraud another and thereby sin all too greatly.
div.note: X reads ‘he’; Liebermann prints ‘[b]e’. A stray character and line breaks inside K were tidied. Liebermann compares 12.

Zu fare vgl.: fór Geþyncðo 1. Geradezu Gesetzsprecheramt oder doch Rechtweisung scheint hier dem Bischofe zugeschrieben.—‘Landrecht’ hier ‘Hundred- und Gutsrecht’.—Q setzt für diht(an) auch 9. 11 dictio(-tare)

On fare cf.: fór Geþyncðo 1. What is ascribed to the bishop here seems to be virtually the office of lawspeaker, or at any rate the declaring of the law.—‘Landrecht’ here means ‘hundred and manorial law’.—For diht(an) Q also puts dictio(-tare) in 9. 11
